claims.claim: Full-length γC4 can mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface by coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh.
claims.source: However, γC41–4 behaved as a very weak dimer in AUC (KD >500 μM; Figure 2—source data 1), nevertheless full-length γC4 can mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface by coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh (Thu et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Two distinct crystal forms of γC4EC1–4 were obtained, one at 2.4 Å resolution and the other with anisotropic diffraction at 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å resolution.
claims.source: We therefore sought to crystallize a mouse C-type cPcdh engaged in a trans interaction and obtained two distinct crystal forms of γC4EC1–4, one at 2.4 Å resolution (crystallized at pH 7.5) and the other with anisotropic diffraction at 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å resolution (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, Figure 3—source data 1) (crystallized at pH 6.0).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, and Figure 3—source data 1.

claims.claim: Both γC4EC1–4 crystal structures revealed an EC1–4-mediated head-to-tail trans dimer.
claims.source: Both crystal structures revealed an EC1–4-mediated head-to-tail trans dimer: The 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å crystal structure appears to have a fully intact trans interface with a total buried surface area of 3800 Å2, which is a similar size to other cPcdh trans dimer interfaces (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, and citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Nicoludis et al., 2016).

claims.claim: The 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å γC4 crystal structure has a fully intact trans interface with a total buried surface area of 3800 Å2.
claims.source: Both crystal structures revealed an EC1–4-mediated head-to-tail trans dimer: The 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å crystal structure appears to have a fully intact trans interface with a total buried surface area of 3800 Å2, which is a similar size to other cPcdh trans dimer interfaces (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The 2.4 Å γC4 structure had an apparently partially disrupted EC2:EC3 interface resulting in a total buried surface area of just 2900 Å2.
claims.source: However, the 2.4 Å structure had an apparently partially disrupted EC2:EC3 interface resulting in a total buried surface area of just 2900 Å2 (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The difference between the two γC4 crystal structures may be due to differences in the pH of the crystallization and its effect on the ionization state of the three histidines present in the EC2:EC3 interface.
claims.source: The difference between the two structures may be due to differences in the pH of the crystallization and its effect on the ionization state of the three histidines present in the EC2:EC3 interface (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations and structural analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The differences between the two γC4 crystal structures could reflect distinct states of a dynamic interaction.
claims.source: The differences could also reflect distinct states of a dynamic interaction, as has previously been observed crystallographically (Nicoludis et al., 2016; Goodman et al., 2016a) and explored computationally for other cPcdh trans interactions (Nicoludis et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference supported by citations to prior literature (Nicoludis et al., 2016; Goodman et al., 2016a; Nicoludis et al., 2019).

claims.claim: The intact crystal form 1 γC4 dimer is similar overall to those of the published intact alternate α, β, γA, and γB cPcdhs and the published δ2 nonclustered (nc) Pcdh trans dimers.
claims.source: The intact crystal form 1 γC4 dimer is similar overall to those of the published intact alternate α, β, γA, and γB cPcdhs and the published δ2 nonclustered (nc) Pcdh trans dimers (root mean square deviation [RMSD] over aligned Cαs 2.4–4.5 Å; Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison data presented in Figure 3—source data 2.

claims.claim: Two buried charges in the γC4 trans interface, E78 and D290, could potentially contribute to the low interaction affinity.
claims.source: Comparison between the γB2 and γC4 dimer interfaces highlighted two buried charges in the γC4 trans interface, E78 and D290, which could potentially contribute to the low interaction affinity (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The two D290 mutations tested, D290A and D290N, had no measurable impact on γC4 binding.
claims.source: The two D290 mutations we tested, D290A and D290N, had no measurable impact on binding; but mutating E78 significantly increased the binding affinity with γC4EC1–4 E78A showing a KD of 58 μM and γC4EC1–4 E78Q, 83 μM (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Mutating E78 significantly increased the γC4 binding affinity with γC4EC1–4 E78A showing a KD of 58 μM and γC4EC1–4 E78Q, 83 μM.
claims.source: The two D290 mutations we tested, D290A and D290N, had no measurable impact on binding; but mutating E78 significantly increased the binding affinity with γC4EC1–4 E78A showing a KD of 58 μM and γC4EC1–4 E78Q, 83 μM (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: γC4EC1–4 S344R had a stronger binding affinity than wild-type with a KD of 112 μM.
claims.source: Similar to the E78 mutants, γC4EC1–4 S344R also had a stronger binding affinity than wild-type with a KD of 112 μM (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: E78 plays an important role in weakening cPcdh γC4's trans interaction.
claims.source: It appears then that E78 plays an important role in weakening cPcdh γC4's trans interaction although the functional reasons for γC4's weak trans interaction are unclear.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claims.claim: Four analytes, β13–6, γA43–6, γA93–6, and γC33–6, are monomeric in solution as measured by AUC.
claims.source: Each of the analytes was also analyzed by AUC to determine their homophilic cis-interaction behavior (Figure 4—source data 1): Four analytes, β13–6, γA43–6, γA93–6, and γC33–6, are monomeric in solution as measured by AUC, therefore their SPR binding profiles could be analyzed to determine their heterophilic binding affinities (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4—source data 1.

claims.claim: cPcdh cis binding is generally promiscuous, with measurable cis interactions observed for 86% of pairs tested.
claims.source: Overall, these SPR data show that cPcdh cis binding is generally promiscuous, with measurable cis interactions observed for 86% of pairs tested (using a 40 RU threshold).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR experiments.

claims.claim: The wide range of binding responses and homo- and heterodimeric KDs span 0.2201 μM to no measurable interaction in solution.
claims.source: However, the wide range of binding responses and homo- and heterodimeric KDs that span 0.2201 μM to no measurable interaction in solution suggests certain cis dimers will form preferentially to others.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and AUC experiments.

claims.claim: Alternate cPcdhs form markedly stronger cis heterodimers with members of different subfamilies, particularly γC3 and/or γC5, compared to their homodimeric and within-subfamily interactions.
claims.source: For the heterophilic binding pairs for which KDs could be determined (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), the alternate cPcdhs in particular, form markedly stronger cis heterodimers with members of different subfamilies, particularly γC3 and/or γC5, compared to their homodimeric and within-subfamily interactions.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: γC3 formed stronger heterodimers with αC2 than with itself or γC5.
claims.source: γC3 also formed stronger heterodimers with αC2 than with itself or γC5.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR experiments.

claims.claim: αC2 and γC5 both form strong cis homodimers with KDs of 8.9 and 18.4 μM, respectively.
claims.source: Of note, αC2 and γC5 both form strong cis homodimers with KDs of 8.9 and 18.4 μM, respectively, as determined from AUC experiments (Figure 4—source data 1), a magnitude similar to many of their heterodimeric interactions of 11.5 and 6.9–18.2 μM, respectively (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4—source data 1.

claims.claim: The crystal structure of the γB7 cis dimer revealed an asymmetric interaction, with the dimer formed by one protomer engaging using surface of both EC5 and EC6 and one protomer engaging using only EC6.
claims.source: The crystal structure of the γB7 cis dimer revealed an asymmetric interaction, with the dimer formed by one protomer engaging using surface of both EC5 and EC6 and one protomer engaging using only EC6 (Goodman et al., 2017) with regions of EC6 overlapping in both EC5–6 and the EC6-only interfaces for all cPcdh subfamilies (Thu et al., 2014; Goodman et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Alternate α-cPcdhs, which can only form the EC5–6 side of the cis dimer, require coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh from another cPcdh subfamily for robust delivery to the cell surface.
claims.source: Alternate α-cPcdhs, which can only form the EC5–6 side of the cis dimer, require coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh from another cPcdh subfamily, which can form the EC6-only side of the cis dimer, for robust delivery to the cell surface (Thu et al., 2014; Goodman et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014; Goodman et al., 2017).

claims.claim: γA-cPcdhs will prefer to form the EC6-only side of the interface since they have a poorly conserved EC5 interface and do not form strong homodimers in solution.
claims.source: We previously suggested that γA-cPcdhs will prefer to form the EC6-only side of the interface since they have a poorly conserved EC5 interface and do not form strong homodimers in solution (Figure 4—source data 1; Goodman et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis and experimental data, supported by a citation to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017).

claims.claim: γA-cPcdhs form strong heterodimers with γC3 with dissociation constants in the low-micromolar range.
claims.source: The C-type cPcdh γC3 also does not form cis homodimers in solution. However, as shown in Figure 4, γA-cPcdhs form strong heterodimers with γC3 with dissociation constants in the low-micromolar range (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4, Figure 4B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Structure-guided sequence analysis suggests that γC3 prefers to form the EC5–6 side of the cis dimer.
claims.source: Structure-guided sequence analysis for the γA4/γC3 dimer in both EC6-only and EC5–6 possible orientations, using the available crystal structures of the γB7EC3–6 cis dimer and monomeric γA4EC3–6 (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggests that γC3 prefers to form the EC5–6 side: γC3 has a number of residue differences in interface residues that are conserved among β, γA, and γB cPcdhs (V/L555, R/K558, W/V562, and S/R595) that seem likely to disfavor the EC6-only side of the interface and favor the EC5–6 side (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C,).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: γA4 V560R did not dimerize with wild-type γC3, whereas γC3 V560R could still dimerize with wild-type γA4.
claims.source: γA4 V560R did not dimerize with wild-type γC3, whereas γC3 V560R could still dimerize with wild-type γA4 (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: γA4 K558R did not dimerize with wild-type γC3 in MALS and SPR experiments.
claims.source: We also generated a γC3-like mutant of γA4, K558R, which also targets the EC6-only interface. Like γA4 V560R, γA4 K558R also did not dimerize with wild-type γC3 in MALS and, when replicated, in SPR experiments (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: The reverse mutation in γC3, R558K, inhibited dimerization with wild-type γA4.
claims.source: The reverse mutation in γC3, R558K, inhibited dimerization with wild-type γA4 (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The γA4/γC3 dimer has a preferred orientation, with γA4 predominantly occupying the EC6-only position and γC3 the EC5–6 side.
claims.source: Therefore, like the α-specific R560 residue, γC3-specific R558 has distinct effects on dimerization when in γA4 or γC3, inhibiting heterodimerization when mutated into γA4 but promoting heterodimerization in γC3. Together these data suggest that the γA4/γC3 dimer has a preferred orientation, with γA4 predominantly occupying the EC6-only position and γC3 the EC5–6 side.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claims.claim: γB7 Y532G had only a small impact on γA4 binding, while γB7 A570R abolished γA4 binding.
claims.source: In SPR, γB7 Y532G had only a small impact on γA4 binding, while γB7 A570R abolished γA4 binding (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: γB7 Y532G prevented γC3 binding while γB7 A570R showed robust γC3 binding.
claims.source: In contrast, γB7 Y532G prevented γC3 binding while γB7 A570R showed robust γC3 binding (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: γA4/γB7 and γC3/γB7 cis heterodimers have preferred orientations with γA4 and γC3 maintaining their preferences for the EC6-only and EC5–6 positions, respectively.
claims.source: These results suggest that γA4/γB7 and γC3/γB7 cis heterodimers also have preferred orientations with γA4 and γC3 maintaining their preferences for the EC6-only and EC5–6 positions, respectively.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claims.claim: SPR data for the γB7 mutants over the αC2 surface suggest αC2 preferentially occupies the EC6-only side in αC2/γB7 dimers.
claims.source: Additionally, SPR data for the γB7 mutants over the αC2 surface suggest αC2 preferentially occupies the EC6-only side in αC2/γB7 dimers (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The results reveal a remarkable level of specificity in trans homophilic interactions since in no case was a heterophilic trans interaction detected in SPR measurements.
claims.source: First, they reveal a remarkable level of specificity in trans homophilic interactions since in no case was a heterophilic trans interaction detected in our SPR measurements.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR measurements.

claims.claim: This level of specificity is unusual for cell–cell recognition proteins, as significant intrafamily interactions are evident in most other families examined to date.
claims.source: This level of specificity is unusual for cell–cell recognition proteins, as significant intrafamily interactions are evident in most other families examined to date including type I cadherins (Katsamba et al., 2009; Vendome et al., 2014), type II cadherins (Brasch et al., 2018), DIPs and Dprs (Cosmanescu et al., 2018), sidekicks (Goodman et al., 2016b), and nectins (Harrison et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Katsamba et al., 2009; Vendome et al., 2014; Brasch et al., 2018; Cosmanescu et al., 2018; Goodman et al., 2016b; Harrison et al., 2012).

claims.claim: The nonclustered δ- protocadherins show heterophilic intra-family trans interactions, though they show no cross-reactivity with cPcdhs.
claims.source: Even the nonclustered δ- protocadherins, which are preferentially homophilic and utilize an antiparallel EC1–4 interface like the cPcdhs (Cooper et al., 2016; Harrison et al., 2020; Modak and Sotomayor, 2019), show heterophilic intra-family trans interactions, though they show no cross-reactivity with cPcdhs (Harrison et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Cooper et al., 2016; Harrison et al., 2020; Modak and Sotomayor, 2019).

claims.claim: High-fidelity homophilic interaction is a strict requirement of the chain-termination model for the barcoding of vertebrate neurons.
claims.source: High-fidelity homophilic interaction is a strict requirement of the chain-termination model for the barcoding of vertebrate neurons and has been accomplished through the exploitation of a multidomain interface of almost 4000 Å2 (Nicoludis et al., 2019) that enables the positioning of enough 'negative constraints' (Sergeeva et al., 2020) to preclude the dimerization of about 1600 heterophilic pairs of 58 mouse cPcdh isoforms (Rubinstein et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Nicoludis et al., 2019; Sergeeva et al., 2020; Rubinstein et al., 2017).

claims.claim: Changing all five residues in β6 to those of β8 generates a mutant protein with essentially wild-type β8 properties.
claims.source: We first note that changing all five residues in β6 to those of β8 generates a mutant protein with essentially wild-type β8 properties; it binds strongly to β8 but not to β6 as seen in SPR and also forms mixed aggregates with β8 but not β6.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and cell aggregation assays.

claims.claim: Most of the single residue mutants of β6 retain β6-like properties in both SPR and cell aggregation assays.
claims.source: In contrast, most of the single residue mutants retain β6-like properties in both assays whereas double and triple mutants exhibit intermediate behavior between β6 and β8.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and cell aggregation assays.

claims.claim: Despite the 92% sequence identity between β6 and β8, their highly specific homophilic properties can be attributed to five interfacial residues.
claims.source: These results demonstrate that despite the 92% sequence identity between β6 and β8, their highly specific homophilic properties can be attributed to five interfacial residues.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claims.claim: The cell aggregation assays are consistent with the heterophilic binding traces measured by SPR.
claims.source: Moreover, the cell aggregation assays are consistent with the heterophilic binding traces measured by SPR; cells expressing mutants that generate strong SPR signals with either wild-type β6 or β8 also form mixed aggregates with cells expressing the same wild-type protein.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of experimental data from SPR and cell aggregation assays.

claims.claim: Intrasubtype cis interactions are invariably weaker than intersubtype interactions.
claims.source: Functional mutagenesis studies have already established that alternate α cPcdhs and the C-type γC4 do not form intrasubtype cis interactions and can only reach the cell surface when mediated by heterophilic cis interactions with members of other subtype families (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014). The data presented in Figure 4 indicate that this is an extreme example of quite general behavior: intrasubtype cis interactions are invariably weaker than intersubtype interactions.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014).

claims.claim: β1, all γA-Pcdhs, and γC3 do not form measurable homodimeric cis interactions in solution-based AUC experiments.
claims.source: This includes β1, all γA-Pcdhs, and γC3 which do not form measurable homodimeric cis interactions in our solution-based AUC experiments.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from AUC experiments.

claims.claim: The presence of cPcdhs on the restricted 2D surface of membranes can promote cis dimerization.
claims.source: We have attributed this to their presence on the restricted 2D surface of membranes which can promote cis dimerization (Wu et al., 2013) whereas biophysical experiments are carried out in a 3D solution environment (Goodman et al., 2016a).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference supported by citations to prior literature (Wu et al., 2013; Goodman et al., 2016a).

claims.claim: Intrasubtype cis dimers likely assemble when constrained in more native membrane environments.
claims.source: Therefore, although our biophysical experiments demonstrate that intrasubtype cis interactions are comparatively weak and, in some cases undetectable in solution, intrasubtype cis dimers likely assemble when constrained in more native membrane environments.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations and knowledge of membrane environments.

claims.claim: α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers, at least in their cell surface transport.
claims.source: As such, while α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers, at least in their cell surface transport, our data show that the remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, although not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data.

claims.claim: The remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, although not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.
claims.source: As such, while α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers, at least in their cell surface transport, our data show that the remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, although not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.

claims.claim: Different isoforms preferentially form one side of the cis dimer.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data in the context of the proposed model.

results.result: The manuscript provides background on clustered protocadherins (cPcdhs) and Dscam1 systems in neuronal self-avoidance, describing their gene organization, expression patterns, and the challenge of generating neuronal diversity with fewer than 60 cPcdh isoforms compared to ~19,000 Dscam1 isoforms.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C22 are well-supported by citations to prior literature and established knowledge. These claims provide essential background context for the study and accurately represent the current understanding of cPcdh biology, gene organization, and expression patterns in different neuronal cell types.

results.result: Prior structural and biophysical studies have established that cPcdhs interact in trans through antiparallel EC1-4 interactions and in cis through asymmetric EC5-6 interactions, with cPcdhs presented on cell surfaces as cis dimers.
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C27 accurately summarize prior structural and biophysical work on cPcdh interactions, supported by multiple citations to published crystal structures and functional studies. This provides the structural foundation for interpreting the current study's findings.

results.result: The 'isoform-mismatch chain-termination model' proposes that cPcdhs form extended zipper-like lattices through alternating cis and trans interactions, with chain growth terminated by isoform mismatches, providing a mechanism for neuronal self-recognition.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C32 accurately describe the chain-termination model from prior work, supported by citations to Rubinstein et al., 2015, Brasch et al., 2019, and related studies. The model provides the theoretical framework that motivates the current experimental investigation of cPcdh binding specificity.

results.result: The study finds that cPcdh trans homophilic interactions are remarkably precise with no heterophilic interactions detected, while cis interactions are largely promiscuous but with relatively weak intrasubfamily and homophilic interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C34 represent the main conclusions of the study, supported by comprehensive SPR and AUC experimental data presented in Figures 2 and 4. The binary specificity of trans interactions and the promiscuous but preferential nature of cis interactions are clearly demonstrated by the experimental results.

results.result: SPR experiments with biotinylated EC1-4 fragments from six representative cPcdh isoforms revealed strictly homophilic trans binding with no heterophilic interactions detected, even between highly similar isoforms (β6/8 with 92% identity and γA8/9 with 82% identity).
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C41 are well-supported by SPR data in Figure 2A and AUC validation in Figure 2-source data 1. The experimental design is sound, with appropriate controls including trans interface mutants (C41) that confirm binding occurs via the expected interface. The estimated lower limit KD of ~200 μM for heterophilic interactions (C40) is a reasonable inference from detection limits.

results.result: C-type cPcdhs also exhibit strictly homophilic trans binding, with each of four C-type fragments (αC2, γC3, γC4, γC5) binding only to its cognate partner and showing no binding to alternate cPcdhs.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C44 are supported by SPR data in Figure 2B and mutagenesis controls in Figure 2-figure supplement 1B. The extension of strict homophilic specificity to C-type cPcdhs strengthens the generality of the findings across the entire cPcdh family.

results.result: αC1 is an exception among C-type cPcdhs, not mediating cell-cell interactions in aggregation assays, and the recombinant EC1-4 fragment forms non-native disulfide-linked multimers, possibly due to incomplete calcium-coordinating residues in the EC3:EC4 linker.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C47 are supported by prior literature (C45: Thu et al., 2014) and experimental observations from protein production (C46) combined with sequence analysis (C47). The inability to study αC1 is appropriately acknowledged as a limitation.

results.result: AUC measurements revealed a >200-fold range of trans homodimer binding affinities across cPcdh isoforms, from 2.9 μM (α7) to >500 μM (γC4).
results.evaluation: Claim C48 is supported by AUC data in Figure 2-source data 1. The wide range of affinities is notable and provides quantitative characterization of trans interactions, though all isoforms except αC1 mediate cell aggregation regardless of affinity (C49).

results.result: Despite varying trans-binding affinities, all cPcdhs except αC1 effectively mediate cell-cell interactions in cell aggregation assays.
results.evaluation: Claim C49 is supported by citations to prior literature (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014). This observation is important for interpreting the functional relevance of the measured affinity differences.

results.result: C-type cPcdhs αC2, γC3, and γC5 form trans dimers via EC1-4, but γC4 exhibits very weak trans dimerization (KD >500 μM) in solution, though full-length γC4 can mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface with a carrier cPcdh.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C52 are supported by AUC data (Figure 2-source data 1) and prior literature (Thu et al., 2014). The weak trans affinity of γC4 motivates the structural studies that follow.

results.result: Two crystal structures of γC4 EC1-4 trans dimers were obtained at different pH values, revealing EC1-4-mediated head-to-tail dimers with different interface intactness (3800 Å² vs 2900 Å² buried surface area), possibly due to pH effects on histidine ionization or representing dynamic interaction states.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C59 are supported by crystallographic data in Figure 3A-B and supplementary figures. The structural analysis is thorough, with appropriate comparison to other cPcdh structures (C59). The interpretation of pH effects (C57) and dynamic states (C58) is reasonable speculation supported by prior observations in related systems.

results.result: Structural analysis identified buried charges E78 and D290 in the γC4 trans interface as potentially destabilizing; mutagenesis showed that E78 mutations (E78A, E78Q) and S344R significantly increased binding affinity, while D290 mutations had no effect, indicating E78 plays an important role in weakening γC4's trans interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C64 are supported by structural analysis (Figure 3C) and AUC mutagenesis data (Figure 3D, Figure 3-figure supplement 1C). The experimental design is sound, testing specific hypotheses derived from structural observations. The conclusion that E78 weakens the interaction (C64) is well-supported, though the functional significance remains unclear as acknowledged.

results.result: SPR experiments with cis-interacting EC3-6 fragments revealed generally promiscuous cis binding (86% of pairs tested), but with a wide range of affinities (0.22-201 μM) and notably stronger heterophilic interactions between different subfamilies (particularly with γC3 and γC5) compared to homophilic and intrasubfamily interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C70 are supported by comprehensive SPR data in Figure 4A-B and AUC data in Figure 4-source data 1. The experimental design appropriately uses monomeric analytes for accurate KD determination (C65). The finding of preferential heterophilic cis interactions is a key result, though the functional implications remain uncertain.

results.result: The cis dimer interface is asymmetric, with one protomer engaging through EC5-6 and the other through EC6 only; alternate α-cPcdhs can only form the EC5-6 side and require a carrier cPcdh for cell surface delivery.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C72 accurately summarize prior structural and functional work (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014). This provides essential context for interpreting the cis interaction preferences observed in the current study.

results.result: Structure-guided sequence analysis suggests γA-cPcdhs prefer the EC6-only side of the cis interface due to poorly conserved EC5 interfaces, while γC3 prefers the EC5-6 side based on residue differences that would disfavor EC6-only positioning; γA-cPcdhs form strong heterodimers with γC3 (low micromolar KDs).
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C75 combine inference from structural analysis (Figure 5A, Figure 5-figure supplement 1) with experimental SPR/AUC data (Figure 4). The reasoning is logical and supported by the weak homodimerization of both γA-cPcdhs and γC3, which is consistent with side preferences. However, the structural models used for hypothesis generation are acknowledged to be approximate.

results.result: SEC-MALS experiments with γA4/γC3 cis interface mutants demonstrate that the γA4/γC3 dimer has a preferred orientation with γA4 occupying the EC6-only position and γC3 the EC5-6 side, as mutations targeting the EC6-only interface in γA4 (V560R, K558R) abolished heterodimerization while the reverse mutations in γC3 had opposite effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C79 are supported by SEC-MALS data in Figure 5B and SPR data in Figure 5-figure supplement 2B. The mutagenesis strategy is well-designed to test the structural hypothesis, and the results clearly support the proposed orientation preference. The asymmetric effects of mutations in γA4 vs γC3 provide strong evidence for oriented binding.

results.result: SPR experiments with γB7 cis interface mutants (Y532G targeting EC6-only, A570R targeting EC5-6) show that γA4/γB7 and γC3/γB7 heterodimers also have preferred orientations with γA4 and γC3 maintaining their EC6-only and EC5-6 preferences respectively; αC2 preferentially occupies the EC6-only side in αC2/γB7 dimers.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C83 are supported by SPR data in Figure 5C. The mutagenesis approach extends the findings from γA4/γC3 to other heterodimer pairs. However, the interpretation for αC2 (C83) is noted to be based on limited data and would benefit from additional validation, as acknowledged in the text.

results.result: The strict homophilic specificity of cPcdh trans interactions is unusual compared to other cell-cell recognition protein families (type I/II cadherins, DIPs/Dprs, sidekicks, nectins, nonclustered δ-protocadherins), which show significant intrafamily heterophilic interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C86 are supported by the current SPR data (C84) and citations to prior literature on other adhesion families (C85-C86). The comparison appropriately contextualizes the exceptional specificity of cPcdhs within the broader landscape of cell recognition proteins.

results.result: High-fidelity homophilic interaction is a strict requirement of the chain-termination model and has been accomplished through a multidomain interface of ~4000 Å² that enables sufficient 'negative constraints' to preclude dimerization of ~1600 heterophilic pairs.
results.evaluation: Claim C87 is supported by citations to prior computational and structural work (Nicoludis et al., 2019; Sergeeva et al., 2020; Rubinstein et al., 2017). This provides theoretical context for understanding how the observed specificity is achieved structurally.

results.result: Systematic mutagenesis of five interfacial residues between β6 and β8 (which share 92% sequence identity) demonstrates that their highly specific homophilic properties can be attributed to these five residues, with the quintuple mutant exhibiting β8-like properties in both SPR and cell aggregation assays, while most single mutants retain β6-like properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C91 are supported by SPR data (Figure 2-figure supplement 2B) and cell aggregation assays (Figure 2-figure supplement 2C). The systematic mutagenesis approach provides strong evidence that a small number of residues determine specificity despite high overall sequence identity. The consistency between SPR and cell aggregation results (C91) strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: Intrasubtype cis interactions are invariably weaker than intersubtype interactions, with β1, all γA-Pcdhs, and γC3 showing no measurable homodimeric cis interactions in solution AUC experiments; however, intrasubtype cis dimers likely assemble when constrained in native membrane environments due to 2D surface effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 are supported by SPR data (Figure 4), AUC data (Figure 4-source data 1), and prior literature on membrane effects (Wu et al., 2013; Goodman et al., 2016a). The interpretation that weak solution interactions may be strengthened on membrane surfaces (C94-C95) is reasonable inference supported by prior observations, though direct experimental validation in membrane contexts would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: While α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers for cell surface transport, the remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, though not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C97 are supported by integration of current SPR/AUC data with prior functional studies (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014). The distinction between obligate (α, γC4) and preferential (others) heterodimer formation is well-supported by the data.

results.result: Different cPcdh isoforms preferentially form one side of the asymmetric cis dimer interface, with homodimerization posing optimization challenges since the same residue must participate in different interactions on each side; however, carrier isoforms can likely fill both EC6 and EC5-6 roles as evidenced by robust cell surface delivery of single isoforms, suggesting side preferences are not absolute.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C101 represent reasonable inferences from the experimental data on cis binding preferences combined with prior functional observations. The logic is sound, though the conclusions about flexibility in side preferences (C100-C101) are somewhat speculative and would benefit from more direct experimental validation.

results.result: cPcdhs from the three subfamilies have been shown to act cooperatively in certain neuronal contexts, though whether this relates to their cis interactions is unknown.
results.evaluation: Claim C102 is supported by citations to prior literature (Hasegawa et al., 2016; Ing-Esteves et al., 2018). This observation provides functional context for the cis interaction preferences observed, though the mechanistic connection remains to be established.

results.result: Possible functional advantages of weak homophilic cis interactions include ensuring diverse cis dimer formation at the cell surface and that homotypic zippers may be kinetically easier to form than heterotypic zippers.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C104 represent speculative hypotheses about the functional implications of weak homophilic cis interactions. While the reasoning is logical, these are untested hypotheses that would require additional experimental work to validate. The authors appropriately present these as possibilities rather than established facts.

results.result: C-type cPcdhs have distinct expression patterns and functions compared to alternate cPcdhs: C-types are often highly expressed (e.g., in Purkinje cells), αC2 can mediate tiling alone, γC4 requires a carrier for cell surface expression and has unique roles in neuronal survival, and γC4 has much weaker trans affinity than other isoforms.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C108 are supported by citations to prior literature on expression patterns (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006), tiling (Chen et al., 2017), neuronal survival (Garrett et al., 2019), and cell surface delivery (Thu et al., 2014), combined with the current AUC data on γC4 trans affinity. These observations provide important functional context for interpreting the binding data.

results.result: Different intracellular interactions likely account for specialized C-type cPcdh functions, with the cytoplasmic domain playing important roles in Wnt, WAVE, and other signaling cascades; for example, γC3 is the only isoform that can interact with and inhibit Axin1; extracellular interactions with other families like Neuroligins may also contribute to functional distinctions.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C111 are supported by citations to prior literature on signaling (Chen et al., 2009; Fukuda et al., 2008; Keeler et al., 2015; Mah and Weiner, 2017; Onouchi et al., 2015; Pancho et al., 2020), Axin1 interaction (Mah et al., 2016), and Neuroligin interactions (Molumby et al., 2017; Steffen et al., 2021). These observations help explain functional diversity despite limited isoform number.

results.result: The study demonstrates remarkable tuning of cPcdh interactions: trans interactions are remarkably specific despite high sequence identity, while cis interactions are promiscuous but with binding preferences; these properties match requirements of the isoform-mismatch chain-termination model for neuronal self-recognition.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C113 represent the main conclusions of the study, well-supported by the comprehensive SPR, AUC, crystallographic, and mutagenesis data presented throughout. The integration of trans specificity and cis promiscuity with the chain-termination model provides a coherent framework for understanding cPcdh-mediated neuronal identity.
